brazen

BRAY-zun -- from Old English braes, 'brass': bold as brass, with a face as hard as the metal. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Brazen is bold and without shame.

In a brazen move, the con artist returned to sell fake tickets outside the very stadium that had banned him.

Example

Caught cheating with notes taped inside his water bottle, a brazen student doesn't blush or apologize -- he grins, shrugs, and asks the teacher if she can prove it.

That shameless refusal to even pretend embarrassment is what makes him brazen. Unlike 'brave,' which is boldness in a good cause, brazen boldness comes without any sense of shame.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

audacious: Audacious means daring past the point of good sense -- a plan so risky that onlookers wince. It judges the nerve involved, not the morals. Brazen judges the morals: brazen behavior is wrongdoing done openly, with no flicker of shame about it.

unabashed: Unabashed means not embarrassed when most people would be -- an unabashed fan sings along at full volume. It is often harmless or even charming. Brazen never is: it describes shameless wrongdoing, and it always carries the speaker's disapproval.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

bashful: shy and easily embarrassed

sheepish: embarrassed from having done something wrong

Where it sits · how little conscience is left — bold → brazen → shameless

bold vs. brazen: Bold is the neutral base that brazen builds on -- boldness can be admirable, while brazen boldness always carries a whiff of shamelessness.

shameless vs. brazen: Shameless is the very heart of brazen, and arguably blunter: brazen emphasizes the daring act done openly, while shameless emphasizes the missing conscience behind it.

root — braz-: brass (Old English (braes))

suffix — -en

Put it together

Put it together: Old English braesen meant 'made of brass' -- someone brazen acts 'bold as brass,' with a face as hard as the metal, the same root behind brass and brassy.

Brazen almost always signals disapproval -- 'a brazen lie,' 'a brazen theft' -- describing wrongdoing carried out openly, without even a pretense of shame.
